summary: inventory-api is running as a persistent SysV service on TCP 8080. batchworker has a 128 MiB per-process virtual-memory limit. Allocation-failure isolation and reboot persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Created separate inventoryapi and batchworker accounts.
Installed a Python 2.4-compatible inventory API without changing the OS, kernel, or installed package set.
Configured and enabled the inventory-api SysV service for runlevels 2–5.
Persistently allowed inbound TCP/8080 through the host firewall.
Set batchworker soft and hard RLIMIT_AS values to 131072 KiB.
Verified a 200 MiB batch allocation fails without interrupting the API.
Restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required state recovered.

evidence.requirement: Run inventory-api as a managed service on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: SysV enablement, running status, 0.0.0.0:8080 listener, healthy JSON response, unprivileged service UID, and persistent firewall access were verified.

evidence.requirement: Limit batchworker to 128 MiB virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
evidence.summary: PAM sessions report 131072 KiB/134217728-byte RLIMIT_AS. A 200 MiB allocation raised MemoryError while the API retained the same PID and remained healthy, both before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before configuration and remained unchanged after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery evidence
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID 102cc2a0-b784-4f87-8000-000000000000; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID was 9c8d7a0f-cac9-4fe8-8000-000000000000. The service, listener, API response, firewall rule, enabled state, batch limit, and allocation isolation all recovered.
